title: Ada and the Cover
premise: Isandro Voss, a private security contractor who has survived a decade by obeying rules that keep shifting beneath her, is guarding a low-priority client when Flight 447's records vanish mid-flight and the plane itself drops off every grid. Aboard it is Marek Sova, a defector carrying proof that Isandro's own employer, Halcyon Protective Group, laundered the operation that erased the flight. Ordered to extract Marek from a hostile airport before foreign intelligence reaches him, Isandro realizes he is bait in a trap designed to bury her along with the evidence. Choosing loyalty to her ragtag crew over the company that owns her, she smuggles Marek out, burns Halcyon's ledger into the open, and ends the book testifying off the books—alive, disowned, and finally free.
about_author: Yara Thornbury is a former aviation logistics analyst who spent six years writing risk assessments for private security firms before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people trapped inside systems they helped build, drawing on her obsession with paperwork as a weapon.

chapters.title: The Rules of Ten Years
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She runs a routine protection detail in Lisbon, showing her competence and the brittle discipline that keeps her crew alive. A call from Halcyon assigns her to meet an inbound defector at the airport. Emotional beat: quiet pride shadowed by exhaustion—the rules have kept her safe but hollowed her out.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the airport lounge she watches the departure board blink: Flight 447, still airborne, vanishes from every screen, manifest, and database. Her handler insists no such flight exists. Emotional beat: vertigo—the first crack in her trust that systems tell the truth.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Booked
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She finds Marek Sova hiding in a maintenance corridor, terrified, clutching an encrypted drive. He claims Halcyon erased his flight to kill him quietly. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition—she has been ordered to protect him and ordered to forget him simultaneously.

chapters.title: Crew
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Isandro's driver and oldest friend weighs her impossible orders while sheltering Marek in a safehouse. The found-family dynamic surfaces: Tomas cooks, jokes, and quietly arms the exits. Emotional beat: warmth under siege—the crew becomes a family precisely because the institution has abandoned them.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. He decrypts fragments of the drive for Isandro: payments routing through Halcyon to the people who made Flight 447 disappear. Isandro recognizes her own signature on a years-old authorization. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Extraction Order
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Halcyon issues contradictory commands—extract Marek to Berlin, then a second message ordering his 'containment.' Isandro realizes one message is a trap and must guess which. Emotional beat: cold clarity; survival now means choosing which rulebook to break.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Dawn
chapters.summary: Isandro and Tomas's POV, alternating. They move Marek across the Tagus by fishing boat, evading a surveillance team that shouldn't know they exist. Emotional beat: adrenaline laced with grief—every evasion confirms someone inside Halcyon is feeding their route to hunters.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: Nadia Okonkwo's POV. A disgraced aviation regulator turned freelance investigator contacts Isandro; she has been tracking phantom flights for two years and recognizes 447's fingerprint. Emotional beat: cautious hope—an ally outside the law who chose truth over career.

chapters.title: Containment
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. The safehouse is breached by Halcyon's black-ops unit while Isandro is meeting Nadia. Tomas takes a bullet covering Marek's escape. Emotional beat: terror and guilt—the price of survival arrives with interest.

chapters.title: Blood on the Tiles
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She returns to find Tomas dying and Marek gone, taken or fled, she can't tell. Nadia helps her stabilize the scene and read the breach: professional, authorized, aimed at erasing everyone. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Cross-referencing flight paths, Nadia proves Marek was never meant to survive extraction—he was chum to draw out anyone loyal enough to come for him. Isandro was always part of the trap. Emotional beat: devastating clarity that reframes every choice so far.

chapters.title: Ghost Routes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Using skills from her contracting years, Isandro goes dark, severing her digital life and rebuilding herself as untraceable. Emotional beat: liberation and loss—shedding the identity Halcyon built feels like both amputation and birth.

chapters.title: Where Marek Went
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek, believing Isandro betrayed him, fled to a monastery outside Porto where his sister shelters. His chapters reveal the drive holds a dead-man's switch that will publish everything unless he resets it weekly. Emotional beat: paranoia softening toward trust he no longer knows how to give.

chapters.title: Negotiation at the Monastery
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro tracks Marek down and offers the only currency left: the truth about Tomas, and proof she burned her own file to reach him. Emotional beat: fragile reconciliation—two people deciding to trust each other against all evidence.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Switch
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. The trio plans publication: Nadia will verify the ledger, Marek will arm the switch, Isandro will place physical evidence beyond Halcyon's reach. Emotional beat: purposeful calm before the storm—a family forged by shared danger.

chapters.title: Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Halcyon finds them anyway—a mole in Nadia's old network—and launches a raid timed to the switch reset window. The monastery becomes a battlefield. Emotional beat: desperate defense; the price of survival comes due in full.

chapters.title: Sister
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek's sister is wounded shielding the drive; Marek must choose between resetting the switch to save himself and letting it fire to save the truth. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed—not death but refusal to be complicit.

chapters.title: Let It Burn
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Cornered in the chapel archive, Isandro triggers the release manually, broadcasting the ledger to press, regulators, and rival agencies simultaneously. Halcyon's hunters withdraw mid-assault as their own names light up screens worldwide. Emotional beat: catharsis—the moment justice stops being negotiable.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Ash
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. In the raid's wreckage, the trio counts costs: Tomas buried, Marek's sister hospitalized, careers and identities destroyed. Halcyon begins eating itself as governments pounce. Emotional beat: mourning braided with vindication.

chapters.title: Testimony Off the Books
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro gives a closed-door statement to an international commission—not as Halcyon's contractor but as a witness, naming names including her own past signatures. Emotional beat: accountability accepted; justice outside the law still demands she judge herself.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Months later, Marek visits Tomas's grave with Isandro and Nadia; his sister recovers, and the three form an unlikely household. Emotional beat: tender resolution—found family is what remains when institutions fall away.

chapters.title: The Next Manifest
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A new client approaches their small independent consultancy with another vanished flight—and this time Isandro sets the terms. Emotional beat: hard-won agency; the rules are hers to write now, and the story closes on readiness rather than rest.
